business: A salon's own staff-and-owner phone app (billing, walk-ins, wallet, WhatsApp reminders, attendance, live floor), set up per salon
by_segment: Established salon with 5 to 8 chairs and 5 to 10 staff
Premium or franchise salon outlet owner, sometimes 2 outlets
Neighbourhood unisex salon or ladies' parlour with 2 to 4 chairs and 2 to 4 staff

why_not: My whole salon already runs on WhatsApp on one phone and it works; asking 5 to 10 stylists to take selfies and type every walk-in's number in an English app is a fight I don't want in a normal week. The cash-drawer and cancelled-bill checks do interest me, but not enough to pay ₹4,999 upfront for software my staff may quietly stop using.

I have one or two chairs and I count the drawer myself every night, so I already know what came in. My bookings and customers are all on WhatsApp and it works; ₹999 every month plus ₹4,999 upfront is a lot from what I earn for something I mostly do with my own eyes.

Five thousand rupees up front and then a thousand every month, forever, for something my register and WhatsApp already do for free. I avoid monthly payments, and twelve thousand a year is real money for a small parlour like mine.

I run one or two chairs and cut most of the hair myself, so I already know who is in the chair and what is in the drawer. ₹4,999 upfront plus ₹999 every month forever is too much for something my notebook and WhatsApp already do for free.

I'm standing at my own chair all day and I count the drawer myself every night, so I already know who's in which chair and what the takings are. ₹999 every month plus ₹4,999 upfront is a lot to pay to watch a shop I'm already standing in, and WhatsApp does my bookings for free.

₹999 a month is not the issue for a salon my size, but half my staff will not work in an English app, and my whole business already runs fine on WhatsApp. If my stylists fumble at the counter, I end up back on WhatsApp and the register anyway.
why_yes: With 8 staff I honestly don't know if the cash in the drawer matches the bills or if someone is doing customers off the book, and ₹999 a month is nothing next to that leak. The first month is free, so I'd try it, though the ₹4,999 setup only feels fair if they actually train my people in the salon.

I count the drawer myself every night with 5 to 10 staff, so seeing cancelled bills, walk-outs and what cash should be there, from my phone, is exactly the leak I worry about. With the first month free I'll try it, and a branded app makes the salon look modern.

An app with my salon's name, WhatsApp bills and a prepaid wallet makes my place look modern next to the other parlours, and I could finally see the takings and the drawer cash without standing at the counter. The first month is free, so I can test it, but I'd make the selfie check-in optional for my staff.

My own branded app on the stylists' phones, WhatsApp bills and the cash-drawer check would make the parlour look modern and stop me chasing the register, and with the first month free I can test it properly. ₹999 is one or two haircuts a month, so if the wallet and reminders bring even a few customers back it pays for itself.
